entries.note: The central claim is a denunciation, not a literal ranking of cons.

entries.test: A representative sample of AI coverage before publication would establish its reliance on financially interested industry sources and whether all such coverage mentions OpenAI or ChatGPT.
entries.note: This is Zitron's own synthesis following the quoted research.

entries.test: Public definitions of user metrics and business disclosures would show whether user totals alone establish profitability, sustainability, or patterns of use.
entries.note: The plain reading concerns what user totals establish on their own.

entries.test: Dividing the cited 11 million paying subscribers by 300 million users and examining OpenAI's revenue breakdown would settle the numerical and revenue claims.
entries.note: The arithmetic assumes the subscriber count supplied immediately beforehand. 'Piss-poor' is a separate value judgment.
No shared threshold distinguishes 'not very popular at all' from popular at these audience sizes.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and documented commercial results available at publication would show whether these apps generated substantial profits for anyone.
entries.note: The surrounding revenue-versus-profit discussion supplies a plain reading of 'real money.' The claim concerns the absence of evidence, not an unqualified absence of profits.
The claim evaluates the revenue figure's worth.
The central assertion judges the industry's scale and financial results as inadequate. Its supporting financial figures can be checked separately.

entries.test: OpenAI's and Anthropic's financial results and inference-cost trends through publication would show whether either was profitable and whether lower inference costs improved their finances.
entries.note: 'These companies' refers to OpenAI and Anthropic in the preceding discussion. The profitability assertion is firm despite the qualified second clause.

entries.test: Financial disclosures and credible reporting available at publication would establish both companies' annual burn and any demonstrated path to ending it.
entries.note: The annual burn assertion is firm; the absence of a solution is qualified as an appearance.

entries.test: Comparable annual financial records for each company through 2024 would show whether its burn increased every year.
entries.note: A consistent definition of burn is needed across years.
'Laughable' is the central judgment. The supporting 2024 revenue comparisons are separately checkable.
He attributes overvaluation to 'vibes and hysteria,' without a shared test for that explanation.
This is a string of insults without a specified fraudulent act or false statement to adjudicate.
'Languished in the same place' does not distinguish technical capability, usefulness, adoption, or commercial progress.

entries.test: Published model documentation and comparative evaluations would establish reasoning methods and their effects on accuracy, latency, and compute cost.
entries.note: The operational account and performance tradeoff are checkable. The aside about consciousness has no comparably agreed test.
The normalization omits the assertion that nobody can explain reasoning's importance. A 'dead' killer-app idea has no shared evidentiary threshold.
'As a result' supplies a causal claim, but 'kind of flailing' has no agreed operational meaning.

entries.test: Altman's public roadmap would show whether it described GPT-5 as an integrated system and withdrew plans for standalone o3 access.
entries.note: Zitron endorses his own qualified interpretation of a public statement. In context, losing access to o3 means losing standalone access.

entries.test: An audit of the linked Fediverse report's citations would establish their authority, relevance, and support for the report's assertions.
entries.note: The following concrete citation criticisms give 'flimsy' a testable reading.

entries.test: Reviewing the public Fediverse report against its sources would establish its factual accuracy, source quality, and research breadth.
entries.note: The surrounding examples make this a concrete criticism of a particular report.
This is an aesthetic assessment of the writing.
The claimed lack of usefulness is explicitly qualified by 'likely.'
The citation behavior is observable, but the sweeping verdict of mediocrity and uselessness is evaluative.

entries.test: Disclosed product revenue, attributable operating costs, and financial contribution would show whether Deep Research improves or worsens OpenAI's profitability.
entries.note: 'I think' introduces an asserted judgment here, not an explicit chance or possibility.

entries.test: Public evaluations of the launch versions would establish Deep Research's citation quality and compute demands and Operator's completion rates and task times relative to humans.
entries.note: The promotional adjectives are evaluative, but the product-performance assertions are concrete.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and independent tests of the products available at publication would show whether they could perform the human-like actions advertised in coverage.
entries.note: The source says the products cannot take the described actions; 'absolutely can't be' broadens that into an inability to become the advertised technology.
This is a judgment of the technology's worth and its promoters' treatment of people.

entries.test: The eventual delivery of the autonomous AI products described in the fundraising promises would falsify the assertion that those products will never exist.
entries.note: Despite the surrounding insults, 'products that will never exist' commits to a firm outcome. The preceding discussion identifies the promised products as autonomous systems that automate work and daily life.

entries.test: Documented AI-bubble-related layoffs, lasting environmental and infrastructure damage, and Silicon Valley employment, investment, and business losses compared with the dot-com bust would test the forecast.
entries.note: There is no deadline. 'I believe will' expresses a firm forecast rather than a probability.
